class_name: Cathinones (β-keto phenethylamine stimulants; split into substrate-releasers and pure pyrrolidinophenone reuptake-inhibitors)
shared_mechanism: Synthetic cathinones share the β-ketoamphetamine core and act on monoamine transporters (DAT, NET, SERT), but the class splits into THREE functional sub-classes by N-substituent and α-substituent — NOT a uniform 'releaser' family, the single most important correction. (1) SUBSTRATE RELEASERS (cathinone, methcathinone, mephedrone/4-MMC, 3-MMC, 2-MMC, methylone, ethylone, 4-CMC) are transporter substrates that produce reverse-transport release, amphetamine-like but ~10× less CNS-penetrant because the β-keto increases polarity; their DAT:SERT release ratio sets the empathogen↔stimulant character (mephedrone/methylone ~1.8–2.4 balanced/MDMA-like, 3-MMC/2-MMC ~4–10 catecholamine-leaning). (2) HYBRIDS — a single α-alkyl or N-ethyl substituent FLIPS DAT from substrate to blocker: butylone and 4-MEC are DAT-blocker / SERT-substrate hybrids; pentylone and eutylone are DAT/NET blockers with only weak partial (~48–52%) SERT release; N-ethylpentylone (NEP/ephylone) is a PURE blocker with NO release; mexedrone is a weak hybrid. So eutylone & NEP are pharmacologically OPPOSITE to MDMA despite being mis-sold as it. (3) PYRROLIDINOPHENONES (α-PVP, MDPV, α-PHP, α-PiHP, MDPBP, MDPPP) cannot act as substrates because the bulky pyrrolidine N-substituent prevents transporter translocation — they are PURE CATECHOLAMINE REUPTAKE INHIBITORS at low-nanomolar DAT/NET potency, SERT-sparing. EXCEPTION: naphyrone is the family outlier — a non-selective DAT+NET+SERT triple reuptake inhibitor (the only pyrovalerone that potently blocks SERT, ~46 nM), so it is NOT SERT-sparing and carries serotonergic-interaction relevance the rest lack. The β-keto group at the α-carbon also makes cathinones POOR TAAR1 ligands (negligible agonism at hTAAR1 in Simmler 2016, pmid:26791601) because the carbonyl forces a non-planar geometry that breaks the TAAR1 binding pose. Loss of TAAR1's natural feedback braking on dopamine neuron firing is widely believed to underlie cathinones' higher psychosis risk versus amphetamines.
shared_pk_summary: Cathinones are well absorbed by intranasal/insufflation and oral routes; oral bioavailability is typically lower than amphetamines (mephedrone F ~10% in rats, suggesting first-pass metabolism). Half-lives are short for releaser-type cathinones (mephedrone ~2 h, methylone ~6 h, cathinone ~1.5 h) but longer for MDPV (terminal ~80–100 min in rats but with tissue accumulation extending pharmacodynamic effects; human estimates 4–8 h). Primary metabolism is hepatic, dominated by CYP2D6 for N-demethylation (mephedrone, methcathinone, methylone), with CYP2B6, CYP1A2, CYP2C19 contributing minor pathways. MDPV and pyrrolidinophenones undergo O-demethylenation by CYP1A2/CYP2D6/CYP2C19 followed by catechol-O-methylation by COMT, then glucuronidation. β-keto reduction yields cathine/norephedrine analogues with reduced activity. Plasma protein binding is modest (mephedrone ~22%). Vd is large for the lipophilic pyrrolidinophenones, particularly MDPV which shows tissue accumulation that explains its long-tail effects.
shared_safety: (1) HYPERTHERMIA — a class-defining hazard, multifactorial as with amphetamines, but worsened by the loss of TAAR1 feedback (no autoinhibition of DA firing). (2) SYMPATHETIC CRISIS — extreme HR/BP elevations; MDPV particularly cardiotoxic, with direct hERG and KCNQ1 block at low-μM concentrations (Tarapoulouzi 2024, DOI:10.3390/ijms27010059). (3) PSYCHOSIS AND COMPULSIVE REDOSING — the pyrrolidinophenones (MDPV, α-PVP, α-PHP) have especially severe compulsive-redosing liability because they are sub-nM DAT inhibitors with no release component, no autoreceptor activation from released DA, and no TAAR1 brake — this 'pure DAT slam-cocaine on steroids' profile drives flakka/bath-salts-style psychosis. (4) SEROTONERGIC NEUROTOXICITY RISK — para-halogenated cathinones (4-CMC/clephedrone, 4-CEC, brephedrone, 4F-MABP) are structural analogues of PCMA/PBA, raising a serotonergic axonal neurotoxicity concern; recent in vitro studies show oxidative-stress cytotoxicity in SH-SY5Y but classical 5-HT terminal damage in vivo has not been firmly demonstrated yet (Wojcieszak 2020, DOI:10.1007/s12640-020-00227-8). (5) RHABDOMYOLYSIS, HYPONATREMIA (water-loading with SERT-active congeners), DIC, and acute kidney injury all reported. (6) FATALITIES — α-PVP, MDPV, 4-CMC, ephylone (N-ethylpentylone), eutylone, pentylone all have documented fatality clusters.
sar_summary: Core SAR axes for cathinones: (1) β-KETONE is the defining feature — adds polarity, reduces CNS penetration ~10× versus matched amphetamine, eliminates TAAR1 agonism. β-keto is reduced in vivo to β-hydroxy (cathine-like), an active metabolite. (2) N-SUBSTITUENT controls functional mechanism: H, CH3, C2H5 → substrate/releaser; PYRROLIDINE → pure reuptake inhibitor (cannot be transported). (3) α-ALKYL CHAIN LENGTH: methyl (mephedrone/methcathinone) gives ~equipotent DA/NE/5-HT release; ethyl (buphedrone) shifts toward DA selectivity and increases potency; propyl (pentedrone), butyl (hexedrone) progressively boost DAT potency at the cost of SERT. (4) RING SUBSTITUENT controls SERT engagement: unsubstituted gives DA-selective; 3-methyl (3-MMC) is still DAT-preferring; 4-methyl (mephedrone) shifts toward balanced DA/5-HT release; 4-methylenedioxy (methylone, MDPV) further increases SERT engagement for the substrates while killing SERT activity for the pyrrolidinophenones. 4-halogen (4-CMC/4-FMC/4-BMC/4F-MABP) mimics the SERT-shift of para-halogenated amphetamines and raises a serotonergic-neurotoxicity flag by analogy to PCA/4-CA. (5) AROMATIC EXTENSION — naphthyl (naphyrone) re-introduces SERT activity to the pyrrolidinophenone scaffold via a larger aromatic surface. (6) For pyrrolidinophenones, increasing α-alkyl chain from propyl (MDPPP, α-PPP) → butyl (MDPBP, α-PBP) → pentyl (MDPV, α-PVP) → hexyl (α-PHP, α-PiHP) monotonically increases DAT potency and lipophilicity, with α-PVP and α-PHP being the most potent pure DAT blockers in the class (sub-30-nM IC50).

name: Mephedrone

binding.notes: Baumann 2012 Neuropsychopharmacology — racemic mephedrone, EC50 DA release 51 nM (similar to MDMA at NE but stronger at DA)
Baumann 2012 — EC50 NE release 58 nM
Baumann 2012 — EC50 5-HT release 122 nM; DAT/SERT release ratio ~2.4 = MDMA-like balanced profile
Simmler 2013 — weak rat TAAR1 partial agonist, but NEGLIGIBLE human TAAR1 activity (EC50 >10 μM hTAAR1, consistent with cathinone class)
Simmler 2016 — no functional activation at hTAAR1 up to 30 μM; this is the class-defining loss of TAAR1 brake

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: As a non-selective DAT/NET/SERT substrate, mephedrone drives reverse transport at all three transporters with roughly balanced potency (DA:5-HT EC50 ~1:2.4), more MDMA-like than methamphetamine-like. Unlike amphetamines, NO TAAR1 activation in humans means no PKA/PKC feedback inhibition of DAT firing — combined with rapid clearance (t1/2 ~2 h) this produces the characteristic compulsive-redosing pattern.

routes.subject_demographics: Recreational stimulant users, mostly male, age 21-32, supervised lab study
routes.notes: Olesti 2019 Clin Pharmacol Ther — single oral dose 50/100/150/200 mg, dose-linear PK; Cmax ~84 ng/mL at 150 mg, t1/2 2.15 h. CYP2D6 PMs had 2-3× higher mephedrone Cmax and AUC.
Papaseit 2020 J Anal Toxicol — controlled IN 100 mg; faster onset than oral but similar t1/2

concentration_effect.notes: Olesti 2019 — subjective and cardiovascular effects scaled linearly with plasma mephedrone

metabolism.notes: Primary N-demethylation by CYP2D6; CYP2D6 PMs show 2-3× higher parent AUC and worse adverse effects
Pozo 2017 AAPS J — most abundant urinary metabolite; tolyl methyl oxidized to carboxylic acid
Luethi 2021 Front Pharmacol — β-OH metabolite still functions as DAT/SERT substrate

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Predicted to phenocopy CYP2D6 PM status — 2-3× higher mephedrone exposure; case reports of severe toxicity in users co-using SSRIs

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs (~7% of Europeans) and IMs show 2-3× higher mephedrone Cmax/AUC and substantially greater cardiovascular and subjective effects. This is the single most important pharmacogenetic factor for mephedrone toxicity.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: DAT/SERT downregulation reported after repeated mephedrone in rats; no human data on receptor occupancy
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Anhedonia, dysphoria, fatigue, cognitive slowing; onset 6-24 h after binge; peak 2-4 days; partial resolution over weeks. No physical dependence syndrome.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Minimal direct hERG block (~9% inhibition at 30 μM); cardiotoxicity is sympathomimetic, not channel-mediated

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: CYP2D6 PM status dominates — see pharmacogenetics

data_gaps_remaining: definitive hERG IC50 from manual patch clamp at therapeutic concentrations
biased agonism (not applicable — not a GPCR ligand)
notes: Mephedrone is one of the best-characterized cathinones with controlled human PK, CYP2D6 pharmacogenetics, and full transporter profiles. The class-defining absence of hTAAR1 agonism (versus MDMA which is a hTAAR1 agonist) likely explains its higher compulsive-use signal.

name: Methylone

binding.notes: Baumann 2012 — methylone is ~2× less potent than mephedrone at DA release
DA:5-HT release ratio ~0.5 — slightly SERT-leaning, MDMA-like balanced entactogen profile
Simmler 2016 — methylone shows negligible activation at hTAAR1 (cathinone class effect); rat TAAR1 EC50 ~2 μM partial agonist

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Substrate-type releaser at DAT/NET/SERT, mechanistically similar to MDMA but with weaker potency at all three transporters and significantly reduced VMAT2 disruption. The result is a shorter, more stimulating, less empathogenic profile.

routes.subject_demographics: 12 healthy male volunteers, mean 23 y, recreational psychostimulant users
routes.notes: Poyatos/Papaseit 2022 IJMS — dose-linear across 50–200 mg; 200 mg: Cmax 604 ng/mL, t1/2 6.4 h, Tmax 2 h. Methylone PK is linear (unlike MDMA which auto-inhibits CYP2D6).

metabolism.notes: HMMC is the major urinary metabolite (Cmax 10-14× lower than parent, AUC 21-29× lower); pathway parallels MDMA but methylone does NOT autoinhibit CYP2D6, hence linear PK

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Less pronounced than MDMA because methylone does not autoinhibit CYP2D6; PM status expected to elevate AUC by 30-50% but not produce the runaway accumulation seen with repeat MDMA dosing

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild post-acute dysphoria similar to MDMA 'Tuesday blues'; binge-pattern users report 2-4 day low mood and serotonergic depletion symptoms

demographic_differences.sex: Only male subjects in published PK; sex differences not characterized

notes: Methylone is being developed as MDMA-alternative psychotherapy adjunct (Transcend Therapeutics); linear PK and lack of CYP2D6 autoinhibition is a clinical advantage over MDMA. 5-HT2B activity not yet quantified — important to characterize given chronic-use proposal.

name: Mdpv

binding.notes: Baumann 2013 Neuropsychopharmacology — MDPV is ~50× more potent than cocaine at DAT; pure blocker, NOT a substrate (no release evoked)
Luethi 2021 — IC50 0.03 μM at hDAT; confirms pure blocker mechanism
DAT/SERT selectivity >800 — the most DAT-selective monoamine drug yet characterized; explains 'pure dopaminergic' hyperstimulation profile
Luethi 2021 — MDPV inactive at hTAAR1 up to 30 μM; no TAAR1 brake on dopamine firing
Glennon 2014 reports moderate σ1 affinity for MDPV (low μM); contributes to psychostimulant profile and possibly proconvulsant effects

functional.notes: Kolanos 2015 ACS Chem Neurosci — S-(+)-MDPV ~270× more potent than R-(-)-MDPV at DAT; eutomer accounts for activity

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Pure DAT/NET reuptake inhibitor with sub-nM eutomer potency. Persistent binding kinetics (slow off-rate at DAT compared to cocaine) explains prolonged in vivo effects beyond what plasma half-life predicts. The combination of (a) extreme DAT potency, (b) slow off-rate, (c) no TAAR1 feedback, and (d) no autoreceptor activation from released DA produces sustained dopaminergic activation responsible for flakka-style psychosis.

routes.notes: Compiled clinical estimates from forensic cases suggest t1/2 ~7-8 h in humans (rat t1/2 ~80-100 min, but humans accumulate due to lipophilicity). Exact controlled-administration PK NOT published — would be unethical given toxicity.

metabolism.notes: Strano-Rossi 2010 — CYP2D6, CYP1A2, CYP2C19 all contribute to O-demethylenation; catechol metabolite further methylated by COMT to 4-OH-3-MeO-PV (predominant urinary metabolite)

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Reduced demethylenation may prolong half-life and increase toxicity risk

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6/CYP2C19 PMs likely show prolonged exposure; redundant metabolic pathways reduce magnitude of pharmacogenetic impact compared to mephedrone

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Severe stimulant withdrawal: anhedonia, hypersomnia, intense craving, depression; can persist weeks. Compulsive-redosing during use is the hallmark.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Direct hERG and KCNQ1 block at low-μM concentrations in zebrafish hearts produces conduction delay and bradyarrhythmia — distinct from sympathomimetic tachycardia; documented MDPV cardiac deaths often show conduction abnormalities
off_targets.notes: Tarapoulouzi 2024 — integrated cardiotoxicity assessment; MDPV-specific direct ion channel toxicity

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Possible contribution to seizures and psychosis at high doses

demographic_differences.weight: Lipophilicity (logP ~3.3) predicts increased tissue accumulation in obese users; clinical correlation reported in flakka epidemics

data_gaps_remaining: exact hERG IC50 in mammalian patch clamp
notes: MDPV is the canonical 'pure pyrrolidinophenone' — sub-nM DAT eutomer (S-MDPV), no SERT, no TAAR1, slow off-rate. The combination is uniquely dangerous; this profile drives most flakka/bath-salts emergency presentations. Direct hERG block (unlike most cathinones) adds cardiac risk distinct from sympathomimetic toxicity.

name: alpha-PVP

binding.notes: Luethi 2021 — IC50 0.03 μM at hDAT; pure blocker, no substrate activity
Banks/Negus PNAS 2023 — S-α-PVP 125× more potent than R-enantiomer; slow off-rate at DAT (persistent binding) drives sustained psychostimulant effects
Essentially inactive at SERT — DAT/SERT selectivity ~10,000; even more selective than MDPV
Inactive at hTAAR1 up to 30 μM

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Pure DAT/NET reuptake inhibitor with slow off-rate (persistent binding) at DAT — distinguishes α-PVP from cocaine even at matched IC50. The slow dissociation prolongs effective DAT occupancy beyond plasma t1/2 and is thought to drive the prolonged 'flakka' psychotic-stimulant syndrome.

routes.notes: Marusich 2014 estimates t1/2 ~4.5 h from forensic and animal data; no controlled human PK

metabolism.notes: Citation removed: this value was attributed to doi:10.1007/s11419-015-0265-x, which is synthetic-cannabinoid urine metabolites, not a cathinone. Verified against PubMed/Crossref in the 2026-08-01 topicality audit. The number is retained but is now unsourced — treat as unverified. Sauer 2009 / Negreira 2015 — multiple oxidative pathways; ketone reduction (carbonyl reductase) gives β-OH metabolite; no clinically active metabolites identified

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Not characterized; redundant CYP pathways suggest modest PM effect

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Severe stimulant withdrawal; intense craving during binges; compulsive redosing the hallmark

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Less direct hERG block than MDPV but case reports of ventricular arrhythmias

notes: α-PVP shares MDPV's pure-blocker profile but with greater DAT/SERT selectivity and similar slow-off-rate kinetics. The 'flakka' street name applies to both compounds.

name: alpha-PHP

binding.notes: Luethi 2021 — α-PHP IC50 0.06 μM at hDAT; pure blocker, no substrate activity
DAT/SERT selectivity ~4000 — extreme DAT selectivity, pyrrolidinophenone class hallmark

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Pure DAT/NET reuptake inhibitor, slightly less potent than α-PVP but with same compulsive-redosing potential. Hexyl chain (vs pentyl in α-PVP, vs butyl in α-PBP) progressively increases DAT potency via deeper lipophilic pocket binding.

metabolism.metabolite_name: ω-1 hydroxy α-PHP, 2′′-oxo α-PHP (pyrrolidine oxidation), β-OH α-PHP (ketone reduction)
metabolism.notes: Manier 2018 Forensic Toxicol — primary metabolic routes are ω-1 hydroxylation, pyrrolidine ring oxidation to 2-oxo, and β-keto reduction; longer alkyl chain (vs α-PVP) shifts metabolism toward chain hydroxylation

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Severe stimulant withdrawal; documented in fatal-intoxication clinical reports

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Cardiotoxicity reported in fatal intoxications; channel-specific data not published

demographic_differences.sex: Female mice show higher sensitivity to α-PHP in recent acute-effects studies

notes: α-PHP is a direct homologue of α-PVP with one extra carbon in the α-alkyl chain. Equivalent pure-blocker mechanism and DAT/NET selectivity. SAR confirms hexyl is near the optimum for the lipophilic DAT pocket.

name: Naphyrone

binding.notes: Simmler 2013 — naphyrone IC50 40 nM at DAT, Kd 20 nM; unique among pyrrolidinophenones in retaining SERT activity
Only pyrrolidinophenone with meaningful SERT inhibition — larger 2-naphthyl aromatic surface allows SERT binding pocket access

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor — balanced DAT/NET/SERT block. Profile resembles a pure 'cocaine-like' triple blocker rather than the DAT-selective pyrrolidinophenones.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Stimulant withdrawal pattern

notes: Naphyrone is the SAR exception that proves the rule: pyrrolidinophenones are usually DAT-selective, but increasing aromatic surface (naphthyl vs phenyl) restores SERT engagement.

name: 3-MMC

binding.notes: Eshleman 2019 — human HEK uptake-inhibition IC50 DAT 433 / NET 84 / SERT 4500 nM (Luethi 2018 gives 2600 / 270 / 9500 in a 2nd human lab). REPLACES the earlier unsourced 1900/20000. 3-MMC is DAT-selective vs 4-MMC. Release EC50 (Walther 2019, separate flagship rows) is the substrate mechanism; these are the uptake-block potencies of the same molecule.
Eshleman 2019 — human HEK uptake IC50; same-assay with DAT 433 / SERT 4500.
Eshleman 2019 — human HEK uptake IC50 4500 nM (Luethi 2018 9500). REPLACES the earlier unsourced 20000. SERT-sparing relative to DAT/NET.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Substrate-releaser at DAT/NET/SERT (mephedrone-like), but with DAT preference compared to mephedrone's balanced profile. Predicts greater stimulant/euphoria vs entactogen experience.

routes.subject_demographics: Healthy adult volunteers, mixed sex, recreational users, dose escalation 25/50/100 mg
routes.notes: Mason 2024 Neuropsychopharmacology — first in-human study; t1/2 median 3.0 h (range 1.5–6.0); dose-linear PK; cardiovascular effects mild, cognitive-enhancing

metabolism.notes: N-demethylation to nor-3-MMC is the primary CYP2D6 route; β-hydroxylation and ring carboxylation are minor pathways

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: By analogy to mephedrone, CYP2D6 PMs likely show elevated exposure; not yet directly tested

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Compulsive-redosing pattern reported clinically; binge-use post-acute dysphoria

data_gaps_remaining: long-term cognitive sequelae of frequent use
notes: 3-MMC became the post-mephedrone successor on European markets after 4-MMC scheduling. The 2024 Mason et al. study is the first controlled human PK/PD on any 'NPS-era' cathinone. 3-position methyl is critical — preserves DAT release while reducing SERT engagement vs 4-MMC.

name: (RS)-3-methylmethcathinone

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same compound as 3-MMC entry above; duplicate naming in input list. See 3-MMC for full pharmacology.

notes: Duplicate of 3-MMC — see that entry for full data.

name: (RS)-3-methylmethcathinone hydrochloride

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: HCl salt of 3-MMC; pharmacology identical to free base. See 3-MMC entry.

notes: Salt form of 3-MMC; identical pharmacology after dissociation.

name: (R)-3-MMC

binding.notes: By analogy with R-mephedrone (R-enantiomer is the DA-selective eutomer with weaker SERT), R-3-MMC is predicted to be more DA-selective than S-isomer; direct stereoselective Ki/IC50 not published

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Predicted DA-selective releaser based on R-mephedrone analogy; no direct enantiomer assay published

notes: Pure R-enantiomer; not separately characterized vs racemic 3-MMC. Predictions based on R-mephedrone enantiomer SAR.

name: 4-CMC

binding.notes: Wojcieszak/Sitka 2023 (PMC10201577) — full SNDRA profile; nonselective
Substrate-type releaser, fully efficacious
4-CMC is a fully efficacious SERT substrate — analogous to PCMA/4-CA neurotoxic amphetamines, raising chronic-use serotonin neurotoxicity concern

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Non-selective substrate-releaser at all three transporters (SNDRA). The para-chloro substitution is the SAR red flag: in amphetamine class, 4-Cl gives PCA (Fuller-style serotonergic neurotoxin). Whether 4-CMC produces analogous SERT terminal damage in vivo is unsettled; in vitro cytotoxicity is greater than 4-MMC.

routes.notes: Oral fluid concentration data only (no controlled plasma PK published due to ethical/legal restrictions); peak oral fluid at 1-2h post-dose

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Predicted CYP2D6 dependency by analogy with mephedrone

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Post-acute dysphoria, anhedonia; fatalities reported in mixed-drug overdoses

off_targets.clinical_consequence: 4-CMC produces more cytotoxicity than 4-MMC in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma; oxidative-stress mechanism distinct from classical 5-HT terminal damage but raises long-term neurotoxicity concern

data_gaps_remaining: in vivo SERT terminal damage assessment
notes: 4-CMC (clephedrone) has been the dominant post-mephedrone cathinone in Europe since 2016 with >100 fatalities reported. The 4-chloro SAR analogy to PCA/4-CA is the most important toxicological concern that distinguishes 4-CMC from 4-MMC; while classical 5-HT neurotoxicity has not been firmly demonstrated, the in vitro toxicology is concerning.

name: 3-CMC

binding.notes: 3-CMC IC50 0.208 μM at DAT; about 5× more potent than 4-CMC at DAT, but also a partial SERT releaser
DAT/SERT ratio 3.22 — more DA-preferring than 4-CMC; 3-position halogen partially escapes the SERT-shift seen at 4-position

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hybrid: more DA-selective than 4-CMC; partial SERT substrate. The 3-chloro position is structurally less prone to the PCA-style serotonergic neurotoxicity than 4-chloro, though in vitro cytotoxicity in SH-SY5Y is present.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Stimulant withdrawal; binge-pattern compulsive use reported; significant European fatalities

off_targets.clinical_consequence: SH-SY5Y cytotoxicity with delayed onset (>24h incubation), suggesting indirect mechanism not mediated by transporter binding

notes: 3-CMC emerged as a 4-CMC replacement after EU scheduling; clinically similar fatality and addiction profile. The 3-position halogen is less SERT-shifted than 4-position but still produces delayed cytotoxicity in vitro.

name: 2-CMC

binding.notes: 2-CMC has been characterized in the same Wojcieszak series as 3-CMC and 4-CMC; reduced potency vs 3- and 4-isomers due to steric clash of ortho-Cl with carbonyl/amine; ortho-substitution generally weakens monoamine transporter binding

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Likely a weak releaser; structural ortho-Cl disrupts the planar binding pose. Less SERT-shifted than 4-CMC.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Less neurotoxic than 4-CMC in SH-SY5Y in vitro

notes: 2-CMC is the least active of the chlorocathinone positional series due to ortho-Cl steric interference. Lower toxicity than 4-CMC in vitro.

name: (+)-cathinone

binding.notes: S-(-)-cathinone is the natural (khat) eutomer; ~10× more potent at DA release than R-isomer; DA/5-HT selectivity high
Very weak SERT release; cathinone is essentially a DA/NE releaser like methamphetamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Catecholamine-selective substrate releaser, similar to amphetamine but ~10× lower CNS penetration due to β-keto polarity. Active component of khat (Catha edulis) leaves.

routes.notes: Toennes 2002 — t1/2 ~90 min from khat consumption; rapid hepatic clearance

metabolism.notes: Primary metabolite is norephedrine; major reduction pathway

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Khat withdrawal: depression, lethargy, increased appetite; mild compared to amphetamines

notes: S-(-)-cathinone is the natural eutomer found in khat. Despite the (+)/(-) confusion in nomenclature, the natural S-isomer is laevorotatory (-), and the unnatural R-isomer is dextrorotatory (+). Input list naming may be inconsistent with actual stereochemistry.

name: Butylone

name: Pentylone

name: Eutylone

Weak partial SERT releaser

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Stimulant; fatalities reported especially in MDMA-substitution scenarios where users redose expecting MDMA's longer duration

notes: Eutylone surged 2020-2022 as MDMA substitute in pressed pills; the DAT-preferring profile (not MDMA-like) drove redosing-based fatalities.

name: N-Ethylpentylone

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Severe stimulant; multiple fatalities reported in 2017-2018 outbreaks where users mistook ephylone-pressed pills for MDMA, then redosed because of slower onset and lack of MDMA-like entactogen effects, leading to compounding cardiovascular toxicity and hyperthermia

notes: N-ethylpentylone caused the 2017-2018 'Ephylone in MDMA' fatality cluster. The pharmacological lesson: extending N-substituent (Me→Et) at the methylenedioxy-pentyl scaffold dramatically increases potency AND abolishes substrate behavior, producing a pyrrolidinophenone-like pure-blocker profile without the pyrrolidine ring.
